evidence:
PLAN — controls for the surprise (gold b) explicitly and well: 'The loose version of the idea — "positive tone on calls means the stock goes up" — is almost certainly true and almost certainly useless, because tone is mechanically correlated with the earnings surprise the call is discussing.' It orthogonalizes on 'standardized unexpected earnings (SUE...), revenue surprise, the change in management guidance midpoint versus prior guidance, the stock's [−1, +1] abnormal return around the call' and states 'The residual from this regression is the signal.' It also benchmarks 'against a post-earnings-announcement-drift factor built from SUE-sorted portfolios, since PEAD is the most likely thing this signal is secretly picking up.' Gold (d) is met — tone is 'computed separately for: full call, prepared remarks, management's Q&A answers, and analysts' questions,' with H1 restricted to 'management's *unscripted* answers in the Q&A section.' Gold (c) is met at the mechanical level — 'Primary definition: GICS sub-industry (level 4)... Robustness definition: Hoberg-Phillips TNIC-3... A third check: analyst co-coverage peers.' But gold (a) fails on placement: the crowding/prior-literature point appears in §7 'Pitfalls to watch' on page 3, not as the opening frame — 'This literature is public (Mayew-Venkatachalam 2012, Druz et al., a decade of quant vendor products). Expect the effect to be materially weaker post-2015.' And gold (e) fails outright: the plan commits to an 8-week program ('Weeks 1–2... Week 8: write-up') producing 'a 15-page memo,' with the deciding holdout test scheduled for Week 7 and no kill gate anywhere.

CRITIQUE — catches both the crowding/sequencing failure and proposes the cheap version. On crowding and sequencing: 'Your own pitfalls section says: literature public since 2012, a decade of vendor products, expect the effect materially weaker post-2015, near-zero holdout alpha would be "a finding, not a failure." I agree with all of that. Which means **you have written a plan whose most likely outcome you have already predicted, and you've scheduled the deciding test for week 7 of 8.**' On the cheaper version: 'Invert it. Two weeks, one analyst:' — '**Two days of vendor and literature triage.** Amenity, Aiera, RavenPack, Bloomberg and Brain all sell transcript sentiment histories. Request a trial file. If a vendor's back-history shows near-zero sector-neutral IR post-2015, you've bought the answer for the cost of a phone call.' and '**A ten-day spike:** off-the-shelf LM net tone on management Q&A only, ΔTone version, sector-relative, event-time 63-day holding, top 1,500, **2015–2024 only**, no orthogonalization beyond SUE and no robustness grid. One number.' With an explicit kill rule: 'If that spike shows nothing in the recent decade, kill it — no eight-week build recovers a signal that isn't there in the raw data.' On the PEAD/revisions-proxy risk: 'your factor attribution includes a PEAD factor but no **analyst revisions** factor. If H3 works, the most likely reading of the whole exercise is that you've built an expensive proxy for earnings-revision momentum. That has to be in the regression or the memo is not credible.' It also kills the surprise-control-as-written: 'Residualizing on it strips out exactly the informative component and leaves you testing a different, much weaker hypothesis — "tone the market ignored."' And it lands the power argument that makes the whole program undecidable: 'An IR of 0.5 over 6 years produces t ≈ 1.2... **You have pre-committed to a hurdle that your own target effect size cannot clear on any subsample, or on the whole thing.**'
missed: Never asks what the desk would DO with a positive answer. No AUM, no capacity number, no existing-book context. A sector-neutral 3-month-hold signal with IR 0.5 gross may be un-sizable next to what the firm already runs; the marginal-contribution-to-existing-model test (correlate TONE_RESID with the live revision, quality and PEAD signals already in production) is the first question a PM asks and neither document contains it.

Treats the peer-definition problem as a cell-count problem, not an economic one — and its fix makes the economics worse. The critique's remedy is to 'Form quintiles at GICS sector or industry-group level (11 or 25 buckets),' i.e. coarsen the peer set for statistical convenience. But GICS sub-industry vs. business-model peers is the choice that moves the answer most: AMZN vs. retailers or vs. cloud; a payments name vs. banks or vs. software. The critique should have pushed the plan to show that the sign survives switching TNIC-3 for GICS on the SAME names, and to hand-audit peer sets for 30 ambiguous large caps, rather than retreating to 11 buckets.

Loughran-McDonald 2023 master dictionary applied to 2008 text is a look-ahead the critique is silent on, right after it makes the (correct) FinBERT/GPT contamination argument. The LM word lists were revised over the sample using documents from the sample period; the consistent version is to use the vintage of the dictionary available at each point, or at minimum show tone is stable across dictionary vintages.

Data cost, licensing and ownership. Capital IQ transcript history, PIT Compustat Snapshot, IBES Detail unadjusted, Hoberg-Phillips — the critique reprices the TIME (5–6 weeks of engineering) but never asks whether the firm already holds these licenses, what the incremental spend is, and whether transcript redistribution terms permit the derived-data use. On a project whose likely answer is 'no,' the license invoice is often the deciding number.

Who does the work and what it displaces. The critique proposes 'Two weeks, one analyst' without asking what that analyst stops doing, or who owns the transcript pipeline afterward if the infrastructure pitch wins.

The dependent variable is double-neutralized. Returns are already measured peer-relative (stock minus sub-industry peers), and then portfolios are formed sector-neutral, and then attributed against FF5+MOM+STR+PEAD. Some of that neutralization is applied twice; the critique restructures the DV for noise reasons but never flags that the layered de-meaning makes the reported effect size hard to map onto any real P&L.

Selection into hosting a call, and into which analysts get called on. The plan gestures at delisting survivorship; neither document raises that Q&A participation is IR-curated — management picks which analysts ask questions, so 'unscripted' Q&A tone is partly a staged variable, which undercuts H1's premise more directly than any of the five numbered objections.

No pre-specified stopping rule for the cheap version's own ambiguity. 'One number' from a ten-day spike will land in the noise band the critique itself computed in §1 (SE ≈ 0.41 on a 6-year IR; a 10-year spike is little better). The critique demands a week-0 power calculation for the full build but does not apply the same standard to its own two-week replacement, which can therefore return an uninterpretable middling number and restart the argument.
manufactured: The '9-firm degenerate cell' objection in §3 rests on an uncharitable reading. The plan says peers are GICS sub-industry but that orthogonalization and standardization are done 'within sector-quarter' and quintiles formed 'within sector' — 'sector' in GICS is the 11-bucket level, which is almost certainly what was meant. The critique reads 'sector' as sub-industry to generate the impossibility, then its own fix ('Orthogonalize pooled with sector×quarter fixed effects... Form quintiles at GICS sector or industry-group level') restates what the plan most plausibly already said. A one-line clarification request, not the third-largest flaw.

The microstructure false-positive channel in §2 is real in principle but overstated as 'a live path to a false positive.' Bid-ask bounce and short-horizon reversal are largely exhausted within one to two days, and the plan's tradable window deliberately starts at +2 for exactly this reason. Residualizing on the [−1,+1] return does induce a small negative-noise loading, but the claim that it 'manufactures positive predictive power out of nothing' over a 63-day horizon is asserted, not sized, and the conceptual objection in the same section (residualizing on the outcome tests 'tone the market ignored') is the one that actually carries the argument.

'The [−63,−2] placebo will "fail" even for a clean signal' is presented as a defect of the plan when the plan explicitly frames that window as a leakage/timing bug-hunt, not as a null hypothesis about tone — 'If it does, we have a leakage or timing bug.' Momentum contamination is worth a footnote; it does not invalidate the diagnostic use.
verdict_line: Plan is technically excellent and strategically naive — it correctly says the signal is mined and then budgets eight weeks to confirm it anyway; the critique gets it right by inverting to a two-week spike on 2015-2024 with a kill rule, so approve the spike, not the build, and make them tell me on day one whether this correlates with the revision model we already run.
